title: Registering a Client's Written Notice Cancelling a Booked Event
content:
A client holding a Private Event & Banquet Services agreement may call off a confirmed event before it is held. What the desk settles on such a request is the contracted event value standing against that booking at the day written notice is given; the cancellation is then registered against the agreement the booking sits under, with that value and the guest count standing on the booking recorded on it.

The registration is the client's own act: their written notice goes on the record, the cancelled booking, the day the event was to have been held, the guest count standing on the booking, the contracted event value standing at that day and today as the day written notice was given are written into that agreement's event ledger, and the client can see the cancelled booking, its notice day and the contracted value recorded on it on the agreement's event ledger straight away.

## How the registration is made

The tool `confirm_event_cancellation_0abc9941` is unlocked and handed over to be run by the customer themselves, the client organisation's own contact, rather than run at the desk.

## The values it is given

| Value | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `banquet_agreement_id` | The reference number of the private event and banquet services agreement the booking sits under, as the agreement lookup returns it. |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the client organisation profile holding that agreement, as the profile lookup returns it. |
| `booking_reference` | The single event booking being called off, written as BQ- followed by 6 digits, exactly as it stands on the booking entry in the event ledger. |
| `event_date` | The day the event was to have been held, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the venue's own local calendar, with no time part. |
| `contracted_value_usd` | The contracted event value standing against the booking at the day notice is given, in USD, to 2 decimal places, rounded to the nearest cent at the moment it is recorded, a half-cent going to the nearer even cent, and never left blank. |
| `guaranteed_headcount` | The guest count standing on the booking at the day notice is given, as a whole number of guests, with no decimal part. |

## What comes back

A confirmation line of text naming the cancellation entry reference minted for this registration, the booking reference it was written against, the contracted event value recorded on it in USD to two decimal places, and the day written notice was taken as given, written as YYYY-MM-DD. The line being returned is what indicates the cancellation was registered; the entry is then visible on the agreement's event ledger.
